summary: Discovery focused on private/VPC deployment options for Redwood Private. Customer wants a VPC-isolated deployment with private endpoints (no public egress), cross-account peering options, and region/AZ constraints for data residency. Security and KMS/HSM integration are blockers for pilot signoff. Agreed next steps: share architecture diagram, security artifacts, and schedule infra deep-dive.
topics: Cross-account peering and AWS account design
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-03-11 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Jimenez (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Nimbus - Infra Lead), Liam O'Connor (Nimbus - Cloud Architect), Sofia Martinez (Nimbus - Security)
Recording ID: ff-20250311-nimbus-vpc-01

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya from Redwood. Quick intro?
[00:10] Priya: Hi Maya, Priya here. I'm infra lead at Nimbus. We've got Liam and Sofia on — Liam manages our infra stack, Sofia is security.
[00:18] Maya: Awesome. Carlos, want to intro?
[00:20] Carlos: Sure — Carlos here, I'm the SE on the account. I focus on private deployments, networking, and perf.
[00:28] Liam: Thanks. Quick note: we're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private, and today it's very focused on VPC/networking for private.
[00:36] Maya: Great. We put together a checklist but we'll adjust as we go. High level questions for us: do you require no public egress, cross-account peering, region constraints, and any compliance gating?
[00:48] Sofia: No public internet egress is preferred. Data residency: all logs and inference data must remain in eu-west-1 for now — we might expand later. Also KMS integration required, preferably HSM-backed keys.
[01:05] Priya: And we need minimal networking changes to our existing VPCs — can't re-ip everything.
[01:12] Carlos: Understood. Quick clarifier: when you say 'no public egress' — do you mean the model servers cannot make outbound calls and all inbound traffic must be via private endpoints?
[01:24] Sofia: Yes, exactly. We want an interface VPC endpoint or peered VPC where traffic stays within AWS fabric.
[01:30] Maya: Ok great. Let me walk through our two common private patterns: 1) VPC peering to Redwood-managed VPC (cross-account peering) or 2) Interface VPC endpoints (PrivateLink) into the Redwood service inside your account. Each has tradeoffs.
[01:45] Liam: Can you expand on tradeoffs? Especially around cross-account route table complexity and limits?
[01:51] Carlos: Yeah. Peering is straightforward for low-latency, but scales poorly if you need many accounts or complex route table management — also no transitive peering. PrivateLink (interface endpoints) requires endpoint services and ENIs, and it's in your account so you control security groups, but it can incur per-ENI cost and you need DNS propagation to point model hostname to the endpoint.
[02:20] Priya: Does Redwood support both?
[02:22] Carlos: Yes, we support both. For Private (VPC) deployments we commonly do two flavors: a) Redwood-hosted infrastructure in our account with a peering connection, or b) Redwood deploying a small set of infra in your account (managed service) and exposing interface endpoints — depends on security and compliance.
[02:40] Sofia: Option b sounds better for us if it keeps everything in our account and uses our KMS. But is Redwood comfortable deploying into customer accounts?
[02:48] Maya: We've done managed deployments into customer accounts for several enterprise customers. We usually ask for a cross-account role and limited CloudFormation/terraform templates that we run, or customers run them themselves. We can also provide an ops runbook.
[03:02] Liam: On account isolation — we'd prefer Redwood not to have blanket access. Cross-account deploy via a limited AssumeRole is fine.
[03:09] Carlos: That's standard. On KMS: we can integrate with customer KMS keys for at-rest encryption of model cache and logs; HSM-backed keys are supported as long as the key policy allows Redwood's service principal or the role to use the key. We log key usage in CloudTrail for audit.
[03:30] Sofia: CloudTrail logging is required. Do you support forwarding logs to our Splunk/Datadog?
[03:36] Maya: Yes we support pushing audit logs to an S3 bucket you own, or we can stream to your logging account via Kinesis Firehose.
[03:44] Priya: Good. Now region constraints — our app runs in eu-west-1 and we want inference in same region to keep latency and residency. Does Redwood have infra in eu-west-1 for Private?
[03:55] Carlos: We do. For Private deployments we can provision in eu-west-1. However, some GPU families or capacity types differ by region — we will provide a recommended list (e.g., A10G vs A100 availability) in the architecture doc.
[04:12] Liam: Are there AZ-level constraints we should plan for? Like you requiring specific AZs for placement?
[04:18] Carlos: We can target multi-AZ for HA, but if you have strict AZ pinning we can accommodate but it increases planning complexity and reduces flexibility for autoscaling.
[04:28] Priya: We might need AZ pinning for data egress paths.
[04:31] Maya: Noted. Let's talk about DNS and route tables. If you choose PrivateLink, you'll create interface endpoints in the private subnets and then either set up private hosted zone aliases so the Redwood model hostname resolves to those endpoints, or we can provide CNAMEs — DNS changes are simple but sometimes org governance slows it.
[04:52] Liam: For peering, we'd have to add target routes in private route tables to Redwood CIDR blocks — what's the recommended approach for CIDR overlap avoidance?
[05:00] Carlos: We ask for your VPC CIDRs up front; we recommend non-overlapping /16s or /20s. If overlap exists, PrivateLink avoids that problem because the interface endpoints appear as ENIs in your VPC.
[05:13] Sofia: How about egress for model downloads or OS updates — do servers need access to the public internet?
[05:21] Carlos: We can bake AMIs with required dependencies to minimize egress. For package updates, either you allow a tightly controlled NAT with restricted egress, or we mirror artifacts into your S3 bucket and use internal sources.
[05:35] Priya: Mirror artifacts is preferred.
[05:37] Maya: We'll note that as a requirement.
[05:40] Liam: What's the network throughput and expected latency inside the VPC? If inference is running on GPUs in the same region, do you have numbers for p99 latency for 4k token prompts?
[05:50] Carlos: Example numbers: for a 4k token prompt on an A100-class instance we typically see p50 ~ 150-300ms and p95 ~ 600-900ms depending on model and batching. But with PrivateLink/peering in same AZ it's minimal added network latency. We'll provide benchmark artifacts.
[06:12] Priya: We need to run our own benchmark for our typical prompts. Can Redwood run a pilot in our VPC for that?
[06:18] Maya: Yes — pilot is common. Usual pilot flow: provision test endpoints (PrivateLink or peering), run workload for 2 weeks, evaluate latency/cost/regressions. We'll need an acceptance criteria doc.
[06:29] Sofia: On compliance, SOC2 and ISO are big for us. Do you have SOC2 Type II?
[06:34] Maya: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001. We'll share a redacted report and a security whitepaper.
[06:41] Sofia: And pen tests?
[06:43] Carlos: We do internal pen tests and can provide summaries; for customer specific pen tests we usually coordinate with our security team — depends on contract.
[06:52] Priya: What about data at rest in cache? If using quantized models, where are key model artifacts stored?
[06:59] Carlos: Model artifacts can be in an S3 bucket you own or in Redwood-managed S3. For Private deployments customers often prefer S3 in their account with KMS keys. We also support encrypted local caches on instance storage encrypted with the KMS key.
[07:14] Liam: For cross-account peering, do we need to whitelist security groups on your side? How do you handle source security?
[07:22] Carlos: For peering we provide the IP blocks and we ask you to allow traffic from those ranges on the necessary ports. For PrivateLink, you control the security groups on the endpoint so you can lock down to only specific subnets or hosts.
[07:36] Priya: Ok. Another constraint: our infra team is small — we prefer Redwood to manage more of the setup if possible. What is typical ops responsibility split?
[07:45] Maya: We usually do a collaborative model: Redwood handles the deployment and initial config (with a cross-account role or templates), and Nimbus owns final DNS changes, security group approvals, and signing off on key rotation policies. We can also offer a runbook and 90-day handoff.
[08:03] Liam: Are there any known limits — e.g., AWS ENI limits per AZ causing endpoint failures at scale?
[08:09] Carlos: ENI limits can be a constraint for PrivateLink at very large scale. We monitor and can recommend instance types and spread endpoints across subnets/AZs. For very large scale we often recommend peering patterns or hybrid (peering for heavy traffic, PrivateLink for control plane).
[08:29] Sofia: Let's talk threat model quickly — can Redwood run within our VPC and still maintain separation between different customers?
[08:37] Carlos: Yes. When in your account we deploy within a dedicated set of subnets and IAM roles with least privilege. For Pepsi — sorry, for multi-customer hosted infra we ensure tenant isolation at process and network layer; we can talk more in the security doc. (laugh)
[08:54] Priya: (laughs) ok noted.
[08:57] Maya: Practical next steps: we'll send a private deployment checklist, an architecture diagram showing both peering and PrivateLink options, and our SOC2 artifacts. We also want your CIDR blocks and account IDs to draft the test peering.
[09:13] Liam: We'll get the CIDRs and a list of subnets to you by Thursday.
[09:17] Priya: We also want a clear pilot success criteria — e.g., p95 latency under X, cost per 1k tokens under Y, no logs leaving eu-west-1.
[09:27] Maya: We'll draft the pilot acceptance criteria and include measurable metrics.
[09:31] Sofia: One more: do you support private endpoints for your observability/metrics (prometheus scraping) or do you push metrics to our account?
[09:39] Carlos: We can push metrics to your account as a push gateway or we can expose endpoints behind PrivateLink. Pushing to your account via Kinesis/CloudWatch cross-account is common.
[09:50] Priya: Good.
[09:52] Maya: Anything else?
[09:54] Liam: Just timeline — we're hoping to kick a pilot by end of month if procurement moves quickly.
[09:59] Maya: That is tight but doable. We'll prioritize the infra deep-dive and security artifacts.
[10:04] Priya: Great. Thanks everyone.
[10:07] Maya: Recap of action items — we'll write them up and send over.
[10:11] Carlos: I'll include a short benchmark packet and an example terraform module for interface endpoints.
[10:18] Priya: Thanks, talk soon.
[10:20] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabeling and filler removals. Short artifacts referenced: "private-deploy-checklist.pdf", "redwood-soc2-summary.pdf", "pilot-arch-diagram-v1.drawio" — links to be provided in follow-up email.
